First, recall that:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}f(s) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{s}{(s+1)^{2}} \\ {lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡s}{{s}^{2}} \\ {lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡s}{2{s}^{2}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

- For the first component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{s}{(s+1)^{2}} & =\frac{0}{(0+1)^{2}}=0\end{aligned}
$$

- The second component can be found using a special limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡s}{{s}^{2}} & ={lim}_{s\to 0}{(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡s}{s})}^{2} \\  & ={({lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡s}{s})}^{2} \\  & ={1}^{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

- The third component can be found using L'Hopital's Rule twice:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡s}{2{s}^{2}} & ={lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{″}}{{(2{s}^{2})}^{″}} \\  & ={lim}_{s\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡s}{4} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡0}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{s\to 0}f(s)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1/4\end{aligned}]\,.$

Finally, the limit of $‖f(s)‖$ as $s$ approaches $0$ is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 0}‖f(s)‖ & =‖{lim}_{s\to 0}f(s)‖ \\  & =‖[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1/4\end{aligned}]‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{17}{16}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{17}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
